newsitem.title: FRANCE: Higher savings may limit Pechiney job cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Higher savings may limit Pechiney job cuts - paper.

text.p: Pechiney's cost cutting plan code-named Challenge may generate higher than expected savings and possibly limit the size of planned job cuts, French daily Le Figaro said on Tuesday.

A report from accounting consultant Secafi-Alpha obtained by Le Figaro puts cost savings entailed by Challenge as of 1999 at between 5.5 and 6.5 billion francs instead of the 4.1 billion targeted by Pechiney.
These extra savings would allow a 30 percent reduction of the proposed job cuts. This means 1,700 jobs worldwide, including 850 in France may be spared.

In September Pechiney said the plan may lead to 4,000 to 5,000 job cuts worldwide. In France the job cuts were to come up to 500 redundancies and 1,000 through early retirement. Use of flexible working was to save 1,200 jobs.
The report, which was submitted on Tuesday to Pechiney's group committee said management had under-estimated future dollar and aluminium price levels when drawing the Challenge plan.
Secafi-Alpha targets a dollar at 5.50 francs and an aluminium price of $1,550-1,600 per tonne by 1999.
Pechiney's estimates assumed a dollar at five francs and aluminium price of $1,500, the report said.
Pechiney declined to comment on the report.
